title: KYEC, Nvidia eye Texas site for US AI chip testing plant
source_used: Taiwan News (digitimes is paywalled: only its headline and first sentence were readable)
key_facts: King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), a Taiwanese chip-testing company, announced on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026 a deal under which Nvidia will pay up to NT$45 billion (USD 1.4 billion) in advance for chip-testing services at its future US facility.

The money supports KYEC's wholly owned US subsidiary AeternZ Semiconductor Testing Corp. in building testing capacity reserved for Nvidia; the cost of services is deducted from the prepayment until it is used up.
KYEC's board approved the plan in July, citing US customer demand and a shortage of local testing capacity.
Taiwan News says KYEC has yet to disclose the facility's location or construction timeline; digitimes' headline says KYEC and Nvidia eye a Texas site.
KYEC general manager Chang Kao-hsun has said each facility can take at least 24 months to build.
In May KYEC raised its 2026 capital spending budget to a record NT$50 billion from NT$39.4 billion.
quote_evidence: Taiwan’s King Yuan Electronics Co. (KYEC) has signed a deal for Nvidia to pay up to NT$45 billion (US$1.4 billion) in advance for chip-testing services at its future US facility, the company announced Tuesday.
KYEC has yet to disclose the facility’s location or construction timeline.

King Yuan Electronics (KYEC) has signed a prepayment agreement with Nvidia to support its wholly owned US subsidiary, AeternZ, in building local testing capacity, giving Nvidia early access to AI chip testing capacity in the US...
why_it_matters_hint: Nvidia is paying ahead to secure chip-testing capacity inside the US.
notes: Announced by the company in a filing (Taiwan News). The Texas site comes from the digitimes headline only; Taiwan News says the location is undisclosed, so the summary states both.
